f1.quote: compared equiatomic NbMoTaW with a Re-containing equiatomic NbMoTaWRe film before and after 120 keV He2+ implantation

f2.quote: 120 keV He2+ implantation at a fluence of 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2 and dose rate of 1 × 10^13 ions/cm^2/s for 1000 s

f3.quote: Irradiation and mechanical testing were performed at room temperature.

f4.quote: Nanoindentation used a 200 nm maximum depth, 0.05 s^-1 strain rate, continuous-stiffness mode, and 10 indents per sample.

f5.quote: Approximately 1.7 μm-diameter micropillars with a 2:1 height/diameter ratio were compressed in situ at 1 nm/s.

f6.quote: Re addition refined the grains, increased lattice distortion and excess free volume, and produced several-nanometer-wide amorphous regions at grain boundaries.

f7.quote: The additional grain boundaries, lattice distortion, excess volumes, and amorphous grain-boundary regions in NbMoTaWRe provide defect-sink sites that accelerate annihilation of irradiation-induced vacancies and related damage, suppressing He-bubble growth and segregation.

f8.quote: After irradiation, NbMoTaW showed larger He bubbles segregated and aligned along grain boundaries, whereas bubbles and grain-boundary segregation were not clearly discernible in NbMoTaWRe.

f9.quote: Relative to NbMoTaW, adding Re is expected to improve resistance to room-temperature He irradiation, yielding smaller and more uniformly distributed He bubbles, less irradiation-induced hardening, and less severe grain-boundary embrittlement.
